literal: " Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law.
idiomatic: " Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law."

literal: After Ren became governor of Yanzhou, on parting he said to Personnel Director Cui Xian: "Among the province's men, only Meng Ye should be selected and recommended; others cannot be trusted.
idiomatic: When Ren later became governor of Yanzhou, he took leave of Personnel Director Cui Xian and said, "Of the men in this province, only Meng Ye deserves selection and promotion; the rest are not to be trusted."

literal: " Cui Xian asked Ye: "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?
idiomatic: " Cui Xian asked Ye, "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?"

literal: " He answered: "By nature I am blunt and straight; I only know how to cultivate myself—no other strengths."
idiomatic: He answered, "By nature I am blunt and honest; I only know how to improve myself—I have no other talents."

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Prince of Qinghe Yue was appointed governor of Si Province; hearing of Ye's reputation and conduct, he again summoned him as legal-affairs officer.
idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, Prince of Qinghe Yue became governor of Si Province; hearing Ye's reputation, he summoned him again as legal-affairs officer.

literal: Ye's stature was short; when he came to audience, Yue inwardly despised his small size and laughed without speaking.
idiomatic: Ye was short in stature; at their audience Yue inwardly scorned his slight build and laughed without a word.

literal: Later, upon reviewing cases Ye had decided, he said to Ye: "Your clarity in judgment can be said to exceed what your body suggests.
idiomatic: Later, after examining Ye's rulings, he told him, "Your clarity in judgment exceeds what your stature would suggest."

literal: " Soon he was transferred to administrator of Dong commandery, where he became known for lenience and kindness.
idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of Dong commandery, where he became known for lenience and kindness.

literal: That year, one stalk of wheat bore five ears; the rest had three or four ears on one stalk—the whole commandery took it as a response to his transforming government.
idiomatic: That year one wheat stalk bore five ears, while others bore three or four on a single stalk; the whole commandery regarded it as a sign of his transforming rule.

literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

literal: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, was a man of Boling.
idiomatic: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, came from Boling.

literal: His father Wenyue was administrator of Julu.
idiomatic: His father Wenyue had been administrator of Julu.

literal: Boqian was orphaned young and poor, yet good at supporting his mother.
idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, Boqian was devoted to supporting his mother.

literal: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and appointed him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, praising him: "Upright, pure, and devoted to public duty—a true fine assistant.
idiomatic: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and made him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, saying, "Pure, upright, and devoted to the public—he is a true fine assistant."

literal: " He was transferred to vice governor of Ying province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to vice governor of Ying Province.

literal: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and comforted him: "You have galloped through the Ying region and already won songs of praise; the supervisory office's duties are heavy—therefore I entrust this to you.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and told him, "You have already distinguished yourself in the Ying region and won popular praise; the supervisory office's business is heavy—so I entrust this post to you."

literal: " His clansman Xian was then in favor and power; Boqian had been his colleague and schoolmate, yet except for good or ill fortune he never paid a visit.
idiomatic: His clansman Xian then held favor and power; though they had been colleagues and schoolmates, Boqian never called on him except for weddings or funerals.

literal: Later he was made administrator of Jibei; kindness and trust spread widely, and he changed the whip to one made of soft tanned leather, unwilling to see blood—shame alone was the point.
idiomatic: Later appointed administrator of Jibei, he won wide trust through kindness and replaced the whip with one of soft tanned leather, unwilling to draw blood—shame alone was the aim.

literal: A court noble passing through the commandery asked how the administrator governed.
idiomatic: A court noble traveling through the commandery asked how the prefect governed.

literal: The reply was: "Our lord's gracious transforming power is like nothing in antiquity.
idiomatic: They answered, "Our lord's gracious rule is unlike anything of old.

literal: Then they recited the people's song: 'Prefect Cui can govern well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel.
idiomatic: They recited the people's song: "Prefect Cui governs well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel."

literal: '" The guest said: "If you call it gracious transforming power, how can there also be authority?
idiomatic: The guest said, "If you call it gracious rule, how can there also be authority?"

literal: " The reply was: "Senior officials fear his authority; the common people receive his kindness.
idiomatic: They said, "Officials fear his authority; common people receive his kindness."

literal: " When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.
idiomatic: When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.

literal: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he no longer held an inner appointment and was made administrator of southern Julu; in affairs great or small he always examined them himself.
idiomatic: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he took no further inner post and was made administrator of southern Julu, personally reviewing every matter large or small.

literal: When the people were poor or weak and their cases unsettled, all said: "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry that it will not be decided.
idiomatic: If the poor and weak had cases unsettled, they all said, "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry it will go undecided."

literal: " Later he became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.
idiomatic: He later became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.

literal: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, was a man of Wuqiang.
idiomatic: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, came from Wuqiang.

literal: His father Bei served Wei up to vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.
idiomatic: His father Bei served Wei as far as vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.

literal: When Qiong was young he followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.
idiomatic: As a boy Qiong followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.

literal: Zhi asked in jest: "Do you want an office?
idiomatic: Zhi asked playfully, "Do you want an office?"

literal: " He answered: "Offices are set up to seek men—not men to seek offices.
idiomatic: He answered, "Offices are established to seek men, not men to seek offices."

literal: " Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.
idiomatic: Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.

literal: Gao Cheng, with the rank of palace guard of the fifth order, opened a staff office and brought him in as penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging and commending him.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng, holding the rank of fifth-order palace guard, opened a staff office and made him penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging him.

literal: Bing province once had bandits; the senior adjutant investigated the matter, and all the suspected thieves had already confessed under torture; the owners of the lost goods all identified them, yet the stolen goods were not recovered.
idiomatic: In Bing Province there had been bandits; the senior adjutant investigated, and every suspect had confessed under torture while the owners identified them—yet the stolen goods were never found.

literal: Gao Cheng handed the case to Qiong for a further exhaustive inquiry; he then traced it separately and obtained Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with stolen goods verified.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng put Qiong on a fresh exhaustive inquiry; he traced the case separately and found Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with the loot recovered.

literal: Gao Cheng laughed loudly and said to those who had earlier wrongly implicated the thieves: "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would nearly have died wrongfully."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng laughed and told those who had wrongly implicated the thieves, "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would almost have been executed unjustly."

literal: He was made administrator of southern Qinghe; the commandery had many thieves, but when Qiong arrived officials and people became orderly and wicked theft ceased.
idiomatic: Appointed administrator of southern Qinghe, a commandery rife with thieves, he brought officials and people to order and wicked theft ceased.

literal: If wrongdoing from outside the borders passed through his territory, none failed to be seized and sent in.
idiomatic: Wrongdoers from neighboring districts who passed through his borders were invariably seized and delivered.

literal: A man of Lingling county, Wei Shuangcheng, lost an ox and suspected his fellow villager Wei Zibin; he was sent to the commandery, and after one thorough questioning it was known Zibin was not the thief, so he was immediately released.
idiomatic: Wei Shuangcheng of Lingling county lost an ox and suspected Wei Zibin of his village; Zibin was sent to the commandery, and after one thorough inquiry Qiong knew he was not the thief and released him at once.

literal: Shuangcheng complained: "The prefect let the thief go—where are the common people's oxen to come from?
idiomatic: Shuangcheng complained, "The prefect let the thief go—how are ordinary people to recover their oxen?"

literal: " Qiong paid no heed and secretly sent private inquiries, separately catching the real thieves.
idiomatic: Qiong ignored him, sent private inquiries, and separately caught the real thieves.

literal: From then on people no longer penned their livestock but mostly let them roam free, saying: "Just leave them to the prefect.
idiomatic: After that people often stopped penning livestock and let herds roam free, saying, "Just leave them to the prefect."

literal: " A rich man of a neighboring commandery placed goods within the border to avoid thieves; when bandits pressed him hard he said: "My goods are already lodged with Lord Su.
idiomatic: A wealthy man from a neighboring commandery stored goods inside the border to escape thieves; when bandits pressed him he said, "My goods are already with Lord Su."

literal: " The bandits then left.
idiomatic: The bandits then withdrew.

literal: In Pingyuan commandery there was a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, who gathered followers and had ties to the eastern sea.
idiomatic: In Pingyuan commandery a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, gathered followers with ties to the eastern sea.

literal: Where Qiong's people lived in connected villages along the border, none were infected or implicated.
idiomatic: Villages along Qiong's border that adjoined the bandits' territory suffered no infection or implicated cases.

literal: Neighboring districts at this submitted to his virtue.
idiomatic: Neighboring districts thereby submitted to his virtue.

literal: More than a hundred old thieves in the commandery he all made his attendants; good and ill among the people, and even when a senior official drank one cup of wine with someone—nothing failed to reach him at once.
idiomatic: He took more than a hundred former thieves in the commandery as his attendants; good and ill among the people, and even when a senior official shared a cup of wine with someone—nothing failed to reach him at once.

literal: Qiong's nature was pure and cautious; he never sent private letters.
idiomatic: Qiong was pure and cautious by nature and never sent private letters.

literal: The monk Daoyan was Buddhist superintendent of Jizhou, with vast wealth; in the commandery he had much income and often had the commandery and counties collect for him.
idiomatic: The monk Daoyan, Buddhist superintendent of Jizhou, was hugely wealthy and had many income streams in the commandery, often collected through county and commandery offices.

literal: When he wished to call and pay respects, Qiong knew his intent; each meeting he would discuss abstruse principles, answering with solemn respect—though Daoyan came many times on debt matters, he had no way to open his mouth.
idiomatic: When Daoyan wished to call on him, Qiong knew his intent; at each meeting he discussed abstruse principles with solemn respect—though Daoyan came repeatedly on debt business, he never found an opening.

literal: His disciples asked the reason; Daoyan said: "Each time I see the prefect he carries me straight into the blue clouds—how can I discuss earthly affairs?
idiomatic: His disciples asked why; Daoyan said, "Each time I see the prefect he carries me straight into the blue clouds—how can I speak of earthly affairs?"

literal: " A man of the commandery, Zhao Ying, had once been administrator of Leling; at eighty he retired and returned home.
idiomatic: A commandery man, Zhao Ying, had been administrator of Leling; at eighty he retired home.

literal: In early fifth month he brought a pair of fresh melons as a gift.
idiomatic: In early fifth month he brought a pair of fresh melons as a gift.

literal: Ying, relying on his age, pressed hard; Qiong finally kept them and hung them on a beam in the reception hall, never cutting them open.
idiomatic: Ying, relying on his age, pressed hard; Qiong finally kept them and hung them on a beam in the reception hall without ever cutting them.

literal: People then competed to offer fresh fruit; reaching the gate and hearing Ying's melons were still there, they looked at one another and left.
idiomatic: People then vied to offer fresh fruit; at the gate, learning Ying's melons were still there, they looked at one another and left.

literal: Commoners Yi Puming and his brothers disputed fields; for years it was unsettled; each side cited supporters until there were nearly a hundred.
idiomatic: Commoners Yi Puming and his brothers disputed fields for years without settlement, each side citing supporters until the case involved nearly a hundred people.

literal: Qiong summoned the Puming brothers before the crowd and instructed them: "What the world can scarcely obtain is brothers; what is easy to seek is fields—suppose you gain land but lose your brothers' hearts, how then?
idiomatic: Qiong summoned the brothers before the crowd and said, "Brothers are what the world can scarcely obtain; fields are easy to find—if you gain land but lose your brothers' hearts, what then?"

literal: " Thereupon tears fell; none among those present failed to weep.
idiomatic: Tears fell from his eyes; none among those present failed to weep.

literal: The Puming brothers knocked their heads and begged to withdraw and reconsider; separated for ten years, they then returned to live together.
idiomatic: The brothers kowtowed and begged to withdraw and reconsider; separated ten years, they then returned to live together.

literal: Every spring he gathered great Confucians Wei Jilong, Tian Yuanfeng, and others to lecture at the commandery school; when court clerks had spare time from documents, he had them all study books—people of the time called the clerks' quarters the students' hall.
idiomatic: Each spring he gathered great Confucians Wei Jilong, Tian Yuanfeng, and others to lecture at the commandery school; in spare moments from documents he had all court clerks study—people called the clerks' quarters the students' hall.

literal: He forbade licentious shrines; marriages and funerals were all taught to be frugal yet within ritual.
idiomatic: He forbade improper shrines and taught weddings and funerals to be frugal yet within ritual.

literal: Also, in silkworm month he sent down silk-gauze quota samples throughout the district; military levies and their order were all set in clear forms; as for corvée and requisitions, matters were always prepared in advance—the commandery and county administrators often had not even ten blows' penalty for delay.
idiomatic: In silkworm month he issued silk-gauze quota samples throughout the district; military levies were set in clear order; corvée and requisitions were always prepared in advance—commandery and county heads often had not even ten blows' penalty for delay.

literal: At the time no province or commandery failed to send men to his border to inquire into his methods of government.
idiomatic: At the time every province and commandery sent men to his border to study his methods of government.

literal: In the Tianbao era great floods struck the commandery borders; there was human disaster, and more than a thousand households were without food.
idiomatic: During Tianbao, great floods struck the commandery; more than a thousand households were left without food.

literal: Qiong broadly gathered households in the district that had grain and personally borrowed grain from them to supply the hungry.
idiomatic: Qiong gathered every household in the district that had grain and personally borrowed from them to feed the hungry.

literal: The province counted households to levy tax and again wished to assess his borrowed grain.
idiomatic: The province counted households for tax levy and again sought to assess his borrowed grain.

literal: The clerks said to Qiong: "Though you pity the starving, I fear guilt will fall on the prefect.
idiomatic: His clerks told him, "Though you pity the starving, I fear the guilt will fall on you, my lord."

literal: " Qiong said: "One body may incur guilt, yet a thousand households live—what is there to resent?
idiomatic: Qiong said, "One body may bear guilt, yet a thousand households live—what is there to resent?"

literal: " He then memorialized stating the facts, had the investigation all remitted, and households and people were secure.
idiomatic: He memorialized the facts, had the investigation remitted entirely, and households were kept secure.

literal: Those he had fostered as sons all said the prefect gave you birth.
idiomatic: Those he had fostered as sons all said, "The prefect gave you birth."

literal: In the commandery six years, the people cherished him, and not one person brought a case to the province.
idiomatic: For six years in the commandery the people cherished him, and not one person brought a case to the province.

literal: Four memorials in succession ranked him foremost.
idiomatic: Four successive memorials ranked him foremost.

literal: When mourning obliged him to leave office, gifts from old friends—he accepted none.
idiomatic: When mourning obliged him to leave office, he accepted none of the gifts old friends offered.

literal: Soon he was reappointed rectifier and director of the Court of Justice; court gentlemen sighed that he was held down.
idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed rectifier and director of the Court of Justice; court gentlemen sighed that he was underused.

literal: Master of Writing Xin Shu said: "Upright and also correct—the name fixes the substance; no worry that it will not succeed."
idiomatic: Master of Writing Xin Shu said, "Upright and correct—his name fixes his substance; there is no worry he will not prevail."

literal: Earlier, when Qiong was administrator of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was inspector of Jizhou, harsh in applying the law, while Qiong was kind in nurturing the people.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Qiong was administrator of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was inspector of Jizhou, harsh in applying the law, while Qiong was kind in nurturing people.

literal: Fang Yanyou was administrator of Leling; passing through the province, Pei asked about outside reputation; You said: "I only hear that the administrator is good and the inspector is bad.
idiomatic: Fang Yanyou was administrator of Leling; passing through the province, Pei asked outside reputation; You said, "I only hear the administrator is praised and the inspector is condemned."

literal: " Pei said: "One who wins the people's praise is not utterly impartial.
idiomatic: Pei said, "One who wins popular praise is not utterly impartial."

literal: " You answered: "If so, then Huang Ba and Gong Sui were your sort of criminal.
idiomatic: You replied, "If that is so, then Huang Ba and Gong Sui were criminals by your standard."

literal: " Later there was an edict that each province should recommend the pure and capable.
idiomatic: Later an edict ordered each province to recommend the pure and capable.

literal: Because of his earlier words, Pei feared Qiong would trap him; Qiong stated his wrongful detention, and commentators respected his fairness.
idiomatic: Because of his earlier remark Pei feared Qiong would trap him; Qiong stated his wrongful detention, and commentators respected his fairness.

literal: Bi Yiyun was censor-in-chief; fierce and violent in office, legal officials feared him and none dared disobey.
idiomatic: Bi Yiyun was censor-in-chief, fierce and violent in office; legal officials feared him and none dared disobey.

literal: Qiong's investigations aimed at fairness; those cleared were very many—court and censorate cases began with Qiong.
idiomatic: Qiong's investigations aimed at fairness; very many were cleared—court and censorate cases began with Qiong.

literal: He was transferred to gentleman of the three offices.
idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the three offices.

literal: In Zhao province and Qinghe and southern Zhong, people repeatedly reported plots of rebellion; case after case was handed to Qiong for investigation, and many were cleared.
idiomatic: In Zhao province, Qinghe, and southern Zhong people repeatedly reported rebellion; case after case went to Qiong for investigation, and many were cleared.

literal: Master of Writing Cui Ang said to Qiong: "If you wish to establish merit and fame, you should think of other principles; still repeatedly clearing treason cases—how lightly you hold your life?
idiomatic: Master of Writing Cui Ang told Qiong, "If you wish merit and fame, you should think of other principles; you still repeatedly clear treason cases—how lightly you hold your life?"

literal: " Qiong said sternly: "What I clear are wrongful grievances—I do not release real rebels.
idiomatic: Qiong said sternly, "What I clear are wrongful grievances—I do not release real rebels."

literal: " Ang was deeply ashamed.
idiomatic: Ang was deeply ashamed.

literal: The capital had a saying: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi.
idiomatic: The capital had a saying: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi.

literal: " He was transferred to left vice director and acted in Xu province affairs.
idiomatic: " He was transferred to left vice director and acted in Xu province affairs.

literal: In Xu province city the Five-Tier Temple was suddenly robbed of a hundred bronze statues; the relevant office investigated; neighbors on night watch and those suspected by tracks—several tens were seized and bound; Qiong released them all at once.
idiomatic: In Xuzhou city the Five-Tier Temple was robbed of a hundred bronze statues; the authorities investigated neighbors on night watch and everyone suspicion touched—several tens were seized; Qiong released them all at once.

literal: The temple monks complained that he did not pursue the thieves; Qiong sent the monks away, saying: "Just return to the temple—the statues will deliver themselves.
idiomatic: The monks complained he did not pursue the thieves; Qiong sent them away, saying, "Just return to the temple—the statues will come back on their own."

literal: " Ten days later he had the bandits' names and where the loot was hidden, went straight to seize them, all verified in fact; the thieves confessed in detail, and clergy and laity sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Ten days later he had the bandits' names and the hiding places, seized them directly, verified everything, and the thieves confessed in detail—monks and laypeople alike marveled.

literal: By old regulation the Huai prohibition did not allow merchants to cross at will; when Huainan had a lean year, Qiong memorialized to allow buying grain north of the Huai.
idiomatic: By old regulation the Huai crossing barred merchants at will; when Huainan had a lean year, Qiong memorialized to allow buying grain north of the Huai.

literal: Later when people north of the Huai were hungry, he again requested open grain trade with Huainan; merchants could then go back and forth, each region aiding the other, and the profit of water and land routes reached Hebei.
idiomatic: Later when north Huai people were hungry, he again requested open grain trade with Huainan; merchants went back and forth, each side aiding the other, and water and land routes profited Hebei.

literal: Later he became director of the Court of Justice, but Qi perished; he served Zhou as administrator of Boling.
idiomatic: He later became director of the Court of Justice, but Qi fell; he served Zhou as administrator of Boling.

literal: Fang Bao, styled Zhonggan, was a man of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Fang Bao, styled Zhonggan, came from Qinghe.

literal: His grandfather Fashou has a biography in the Book of Wei.
idiomatic: His grandfather Fashou has a biography in the Book of Wei.
